scope: does a legal phase 7 or an explicit loopback netadr make the connection initialiser send

sessions.name: 20261023-clinit-lifecycle-3
sessions.sequence: install counters -> patch 0x66F20E to 90 90 -> write [0x76446B0]=7 -> wait for the rebuilt cl -> write cl+0x14 netadr -> call 0x5C83D0(1) manually

observations.cl_after_phase7: 0xD362501F (decoded value of the zeroed global, i.e. the client object is gone)

sessions.finding: phase 7 makes 0x77C290 tear the client object down without a successful CL_Init (entry counted, allocation not reached), and a manual CL_Init on the live client still jumps to an invalid 0x102 callback. Manual CL_Init is not a viable recovery path.

sessions.name: 20261023-clinit-lifecycle-4
sessions.sequence: install counters -> patch 0x66F20E to 90 90 -> write [0x76446B0]=8 -> poll cl until it is rebuilt -> write loopback netadr into the rebuilt cl+0x14 -> sample
sessions.finding: A valid loopback netadr written into the rebuilt cl survives for the whole phase-8 window (600 ms) yet ring A and ring B stay at cursor 0. Therefore the missing outbound packet is not caused by an empty netadr: with 0x66F20E neutralised the initialiser simply never reaches the send path. Restoring that callback with a valid target is the remaining prerequisite.

conclusions: phase 8 remains the only observed phase that triggers a successful CL_Shutdown + CL_Init rebuild (create=1), even though phase 8 itself is not a legal client phase and is cleared by 0x77C343
phase 7 triggers teardown without a rebuild and leaves the client object gone
manual CL_Init on a live client crashes at EIP=0x102 regardless of the cl being empty
netadr is necessary but not sufficient; the 0x66F170 callback is on the send path
